text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele and the factions which are expected to form the new cabinet have signed the government declaration. But they have failed to sign the agreement on the formation of the government since it was opposed by nationalist group Fatherland & Freedom. The faction announced it will not approve the declaration until the cabinet's structure, including the distribution of posts between the factions, becomes clear. The most contentious point is the post of Minister of Justice, contested by both the Democratic Party Saimnieks and the Fatherland & Freedom.
- Parliament finally passed the law on compulsory military service. The law provides for conscription of students and university graduates at an age below 26.

- A Latvian parliamentary delegation, headed by parliament speaker Alfreds Chepanis and including foreign committee chairman Indulis Berzins, Janis Jurkans, Ziedonis Chevers and Juris Sinka, as well as 10 the most influential Latvian entrepreneurs, are due to visit Russia on February 16-18.
- The EU PHARE programme has contributed an additional 2.6 million Ecu to speed Latvia's land reform and boost the land market.

- A Russian Foreign Ministry delegation arrived in Riga to explore the possibility that talks between a Latvian-Russian joint committee can be started. They are also to evaluate the contractual basis of bilateral relations between Latvia and Russia.
- It is still unclear at what level Latvia will be represented at the inauguration ceremony of Chechen president Aslan Mashadov.
- Latvian local governments have been given another interest-free loan of three million lats to bridge the gap in their budgets because of failure to collect income tax.
- Riga international airport will collect seven lats in departure tax from each passenger to finance the reconstruction of the airport building.
- The Latvian transport ministry has drafted and submitted to the EU a document with proposals to make Latvia's transit corridor a part of the first EU transport passage.
